# **Decision Log**

This document tracks the reasoning and decisions made while working on the test, so it can be reused directly for the "dataset/schema/approach and why" and "key trade-offs" sections of the README later. It will keep being updated as the project moves forward. Also it helps me keep track of things to do 😂

# **1\. Task overview**

What's being asked:&nbsp;

Build a structured document extraction system (LLM/VLM/OCR+LLM) plus an evaluation harness that proves the system is accurate not just a demo on a clean document, but proven to work on messy real-world documents, that knows when to be unsure (abstain), and that can be reasoned about in terms of quality, latency, and cost.

* **What's weighted most heavily (from the rubric):**

* **Evaluation rigor** trustworthy ground truth, failures understood by kind (not just counted), results comparable across versions

* **Extraction quality** accurate on messy documents, handles multi-page/tables/cross-section fields, no hallucination

* **LLM/VLM engineering** a sound approach, reliable validated output, meaningful confidence and abstention

* **Production-readiness** cost/latency visible, one measured optimization, resilience to bad output

* **Agentic development** effective use of an AI coding agent \+ one custom extension actually used

* **Code quality & communication**

# **2\. Key decisions (made before building)**

**2.1 Document type: receipt**

**Why:** Has a mix of simple lookup fields (vendor name, date) and fields that require reasoning (line items table, total \= subtotal \+ tax)  matches the brief's requirement for "simple lookups vs reasoning across sections." Ground truth is also easy to build manually since fields are limited and well-defined.&nbsp;

**Alternatives considered and rejected:**

**Contract** too ambiguous to schema within the time available, fields like "party's role" require heavy reasoning

**ID document** privacy concerns if using real data

**2.2 Dataset source: Own physical receipts (self-photographed)**

**Why:** The brief explicitly states "**your own scans count most.**" Physical receipts photographed by hand naturally carry real-world messiness (skew, uneven lighting, faded thermal print) without needing to be artificially engineered. Also i already have quite a bit of them lying around and in my gallery so it makes it easier for me too 😂

**Things to note**: All receipts collected are Indonesian-market receipts currency is Rupiah throughout, dates are consistently DD/MM/YYYY. What actually mixes is the language on the receipt itself (some printed in Bahasa Indonesia, some in English, e.g. imported goods stores, international chains, or English-template invoices) currency and date format are NOT mixed. This is being kept intentionally because:

useful axis for eval analysis: does accuracy differ between receipts with Indonesian vs English field labels?

Possible future extension (not in current scope): may add USD or other-currency receipts with different date conventions later to stress-test normalization further. Current dataset is IDR/DD-MM-YYYY only — the schema and prompt should still include a currency field so this extension doesn't require a schema change later, but normalization logic only needs to handle one currency and one date format for now.

Target count: 20-30 own receipts (might increase) with intentional variation and possibly more taken from the internet

**2.3 Extraction approach: VLM directly (Gemini via Google AI Studio)**

**Why over OCR+LLM:**

Single API call per document → faster to build and debug within a tight timeline

More robust to skewed/dirty scans no accumulated OCR error noise feeding into the LLM

Gemini Flash is free and explicitly recommended in the brief

Gemini handles Indonesian text reasonably well (to be validated on 2-3 initial samples)

**Why not an agentic/multi-step pipeline:**

Single-page documents with a relatively flat structure don't need complex multi-step reasoning

A single well-designed call is cheaper, faster, and easier to explain and debug in a live-code session

**BUT** OCR+LLM might still used as one optimization experiment in the Production section, not as the main path so the trade-off can still be demonstrated without adding complexity to the core architecture

**2.4 Language/stack: Python**

Why: Already familiar, speeds up development within the tight (2-3 day) window.

# **3\. Execution Plan**

**Step 1 — Collect & digitize receipts**  
Target 20-30 physical receipts with deliberate variation: some clean/straight, some skewed, 1-2 in low light, at least one faded thermal print, at least one long receipt (may need multi-shot). Keep the Indo/English label mix. Save as receipt\_001.jpg etc. Jot rough notes (store, total, date) while shooting — speeds up Step 8 later.

**Step 2 — Setup Environment and Gemini API access**  
Setup Git, coding agent, env, etc. Get/refresh API key from Google AI Studio, install google-generativeai, store key in .env. Run one trivial test call (send an image, ask for a free-text description) before building anything structured — just to confirm auth, image handling, and rate limits work.

**Step 3 — Define field schema**  
Most critical step — everything downstream depends on it. Write the Pydantic model: simple fields (vendor\_name, transaction\_date, receipt\_number), computed fields (subtotal, tax, total), nested line\_items (description, qty, unit\_price, amount), currency (future-proofing). Decide how confidence is attached per field (separate \_confidence field vs {value, confidence, reason} wrapper) and which fields can be None/abstained vs required.

**Step 4 — Extraction prompt \+ core function**  
One function: image path in, Gemini call with explicit schema instructions (use JSON mode if available), parse to Pydantic. Prompt must explicitly forbid guessing ("null if unclear, don't invent") and require confidence \+ short reason per low-confidence field. On parse failure, retry once with the error message fed back into the prompt. Test with mocked responses first, independent of live API.

**Step 5 — Resilience & error handling**  
Explicit rubric criterion, not optional. Handle: API/network failures (retry with backoff, mark as extraction\_failed rather than crashing the batch), repeated parse failures after retry (return partial result flagged as error, never silently return empty-looking-valid data), and corrupt/unreadable files (validate before sending). System must clearly distinguish "low-confidence success" from "hard failure."

**Step 6 — Sample test & iterate**  
Run on 2-3 representative samples (easy one, mixed-language one, blurry/skewed one) before the full batch. Check manually: Indonesian labels read correctly? Rupiah thousand-separator parsed as float correctly (not misread as decimal)? Date conversion DD/MM/YYYY → ISO correct (not swapped to MM/DD)? Fix prompt now if there's a consistent error pattern — cheaper to fix on 3 documents than after the full run.

**Step 7 — Build ground truth** *(can run in parallel with Steps 4-6 once Step 3 is done)*  
Manually label all receipts in the same schema as model output, reading from the original receipts — never from model output, to avoid anchoring bias. Include at least one receipt with a genuinely missing/unreadable field to test abstention later.

**Step 8 — Wrap extraction as an API service**  
Turn the function into an HTTP endpoint (FastAPI), including a batch endpoint that accepts multiple documents. Log per-request cost (tokens) and latency — needed later for Step 12's before/after comparison.

**Step 9 — Build the eval harness**  
Compare API output vs ground truth: per-field precision/recall, numeric tolerance for amounts, row-alignment method for line items, and a failure-kind breakdown (wrong value / hallucinated / wrongly abstained / misread).

**Step 10 — Dockerize**  
docker compose up serves the API (Step 9); docker compose run \--rm eval runs the harness (Step 9\) against that API and writes scorecard \+ per-document results to a mounted output directory.

**Step 11 — Full batch run, scorecard, version comparison**  
Run all receipts, review the failure breakdown, then run a second variant (e.g. revised prompt) and compare both scorecards side by side — this is your "catch a regression" demonstration.

**Step 12 — Apply one optimization, measure impact**  
Pick one (e.g. image resize before sending), measure before/after using the cost/latency numbers already logged in Step 8\.

**Step 13 — Build the custom agentic-dev extension**  
An actual small tool you used, not just a README mention (e.g. a script/skill that scaffolds ground truth templates or assists labeling).

**Step 14 — Write README \+ final commit**  
Pull from the decision log: dataset/schema/approach+why, architecture, trade-offs, eval results, agentic-dev note, next steps. Commit everything including the scorecard from a real run.

**Step 2 — Setup Environment and Gemini API access**

Initialized git repository, created a Python virtual environment, and set up base dependencies (google-generativeai, python-dotenv, pydantic) via requirements.txt. Created .env (untracked, holds the actual API key) and .env.example (tracked, template only) to keep secrets out of version control. Connected the local repository to a private GitHub remote (Receipt\_Extraction) for submission.

Settled on using gemini-3.6-flash (since it is the cheapest). Also the google-generativeai which was in the requirements.txt turns out to be deprecated and thus changed to google-genai.&nbsp;

Ran a trivial connection test sending receipt\_001.jpeg to Gemini and requesting a free-text description, to validate authentication and image handling before building structured extraction. The model successfully described the contents of a test receipt image. Environment, SDK, and model choice are now correct and ready to move to the next step

**Step 3 — Define field schema**

Created src/extraction/schema.py defining the Pydantic models for the extraction output, plus src/\_\_init\_\_.py and src/extraction/\_\_init\_\_.py to make it importable as a package. The core building block is a generic FieldValue\[T\] model wrapping every extractable field with value, confidence (constrained 0-1), status (present/not\_present/illegible), and reason — this lets confidence and abstention be handled the same way across every field instead of special-casing each one. Used Pydantic v2's native generics (FieldValue\[str\], FieldValue\[date\], etc.) rather than separate per-type classes, since Pydantic v2 resolves those cleanly on its own.

ReceiptExtraction holds the 7 header-level fields (vendor, date, receipt number, currency, subtotal, tax, total) plus a line\_items: List\[LineItem\], where each line item wraps description/quantity/unit\_price/amount the same way. Added a consistency check as a soft flag rather than a hard validation error: subtotal\_tax\_total\_consistent computes to True/False using math.isclose (not exact equality, since receipts round differently) when all three fields are present, or None if any is missing/not present — this becomes a secondary confidence signal later rather than something that rejects the extraction outright.

![][image13]

Verification lives as a permanent regression file (src/extraction/test\_schema.py, run via python src/extraction/test\_schema.py) rather than a one-off script, so a future change to the consistency validator can't silently break one of the three branches — each scenario asserts its expected result instead of just printing it. Confirmed passing:

consistent: subtotal\_tax\_total\_consistent \= True (expected True)

inconsistent: subtotal\_tax\_total\_consistent \= False (expected False)

missing field: subtotal\_tax\_total\_consistent \= None (expected None)

All scenarios passed.

**Step 4 — Extraction prompt \+ core function**

Created src/extraction/extract.py with the core extraction function. Prompt is split into a system instruction (stable rules: schema shape, anti-hallucination, normalization) and a short per-call user message. Used Gemini's response\_schema config built directly from ReceiptExtraction.model\_json\_schema(), so the API itself enforces field names, nesting, and enum values — the generic FieldValue\[T\] structure caused zero friction, each instantiation resolved into its own correctly-typed schema automatically. subtotal\_tax\_total\_consistent is stripped from the request schema since it's computed locally, not something the model should produce.

extract\_receipt() retries once with the parse error fed back into the prompt if the first response doesn't validate. Sample runs now also save their output JSON to outputs/sample\_runs/, so results are kept as artifacts rather than only living in terminal output.

&nbsp;

Finding confirmed against physical receipt: receipt explicitly prints "Inklusif PB1: 13.400" — "Inklusif" (inclusive) confirms tax is already included in item prices, not additive. This validates why total equals the line-item sum directly rather than sum+tax. The current subtotal\_tax\_total\_consistent check (subtotal \+ tax ≈ total) would misfire as "inconsistent" on tax-inclusive receipts like this one if subtotal were ever populated equal to total — needs to be accounted for in the eval harness design (Step 9), since this is a real, recurring receipt pattern in Indonesia, not an edge case.

Extended extract\_receipt() to accept either a single image path or a list of paths (str | list\[str\]), backward-compatible with existing single-image calls. When given a list, all images are sent as separate parts in one API call, in order, with the system instruction updated to tell the model these are sequential overlapping sections of one receipt — not separate receipts — to avoid double-counting line items from the overlap.

**Test run — receipt\_026 (2-page, HYPERMART AR HAKIM):**&nbsp;

**![][image16]![][image17]**

extracted 22 distinct line items across both images with no obvious overlap duplicates, total=253530.0 matches the reference log. subtotal came back not\_present, but this is a missed field, not a correct abstention — the receipt does include a "DPP" line (Dasar Pengenaan Pajak, Indonesian tax terminology functioning as subtotal), positioned away from the total. The model didn't recognize "DPP" as equivalent to subtotal since the term isn't mentioned in the system instruction. Open item for Step 6: add "DPP" as a recognized subtotal label in the prompt, and re-test this receipt to confirm the fix.

Known limitation, not addressed yet: the receipt includes item-level discounts. unit\_price and amount both reflect the correct final (post-discount) figures, but the schema has no dedicated field for the discount itself — it's implicitly absorbed into the final amount rather than captured explicitly. Acceptable for now given scope, but worth deciding later (schema revision vs accepting as-is) if discounted items turn out to be common across the dataset.

Output filename convention for multi-image runs: input basenames joined with \+ (e.g. receipt\_026\_p1+receipt\_026\_p2\_output.json).

**Step 5 — Resilience & error handling**

extract\_receipt() now returns ReceiptExtraction | ExtractionError, with ExtractionError carrying image\_paths, failure\_stage (invalid\_input/api\_failure/parse\_failure), and message — a single isinstance check distinguishes a hard failure from a normal (possibly low-confidence) success.

![][image18]

Invalid input: missing file and a corrupt/non-image file both correctly short-circuit to invalid\_input with zero API calls, before any request is sent.

Transient API failure: disconnected internet mid-run, triggering an actual DNS resolution failure (\[Errno 11001\] getaddrinfo failed). Confirmed the retry/backoff logic completes and cleanly returns api\_failure rather than hanging or crashing.

Persistent parse failure: permanently-invalid JSON confirmed exactly 3 total calls before returning parse\_failure — not re-tested live since response\_schema makes the API itself enforce output shape, making this failure mode rare to trigger organically.

Golden path (2-page receipt\_026) re-verified unaffected; test\_schema.py still passes.

Found and fixed a real crash risk: if Gemini blocks or refuses to generate output (e.g. a safety filter triggers), response.text can be None rather than raising an exception — which would have caused an uncaught TypeError on model\_validate\_json(None), bypassing the resilience handling entirely. Fixed by checking response.text before parsing; a new \_describe\_empty\_response() helper reports the actual reason (prompt\_feedback.block\_reason, falling back to finish\_reason) when available.

Verified via test\_resilience.py scenario 4 (mocked, since safety blocks aren't reliably triggerable on demand): confirmed ExtractionError(failure\_stage="api\_failure", message="Gemini returned no output (finish\_reason=FinishReason.SAFETY)") is returned cleanly instead of crashing.

**Step 6 — Sample test & iterate**  
Tested 5 harder samples not covered in earlier steps: receipt\_16 (rotated 90°, folded), receipt\_18 (same vendor as 16, has handwritten marks), receipt\_19 (has DPP \+ subtotal \+ tax as three distinct fields), receipt\_14 (partially covered by a stamp, vendor shown as both logo that is easy to read and printed text), receipt\_25 (PPN 11%, non-standard rate, receipt folded, text starting to disappear).

**Real bugs found, worth fixing:**

receipt\_16: transaction year misread as 2024 instead of the correct 2026 — a genuine digit misread, not a format confusion. The receipt is rotated 90 degrees, might have some connection to this misread

receipt\_18: a line item partially covered by handwriting was dropped entirely from line\_items rather than being included with fields marked illegible — no trace of it remains in the output at all.

receipt\_16, 18: discount lines shown as a percentage (e.g. "Disc 5%") with no final discounted price are consistently extracted as their own separate line item, rather than being applied to the item they discount. Consistent across 2 receipts, not a one-off.

**Design decisions needed, not bugs:**

receipt\_14: vendor name extracted from a recognizable logo (Family Mart) instead of the receipt's own printed label ("STORE: FMI MART SURABAYA"). Defensible either way, but inconsistent with what a ground truth reader would naturally transcribe.&nbsp;

Decided: prefer printed text over logo inference going forward.

receipt\_16 vs receipt\_18: same vendor, same layout/language, but DPP was correctly read as subtotal on 18 and missed (returned not\_present) on 16\. Likely inherent model variance or because receipt 16’s photo is rotated. Noted, not chased

receipt\_19: this receipt prints DPP, subtotal, AND tax as three separate values, where the printed "subtotal" already includes tax and DPP is the true pre-tax amount. The model mapped subtotal to our schema's subtotal field — arguably incorrect for our schema's intent (pre-tax), but flags that "subtotal" terminology is overloaded and ambiguous across receipts when multiple candidates exist. To be fixed in Step 6: add a consistency check to the prompt — when multiple subtotal candidates exist, prefer whichever value, when added to tax, comes closest to matching total (the mathematically consistent pre-tax figure), rather than relying on label-matching alone.

receipt\_25: vendor name read correctly from printed text (logo apparently unclear/hard to recognize here) — consistent with the "prefer printed text" decision above, not a separate issue.

**Working correctly, no action needed:**

receipt\_16, 18: PPN correctly recognized as tax without any explicit prompt mention — no fix needed here.

receipt\_14: stamp did not obscure any extracted fields — no issue, positioned away from relevant info.

receipt\_19: folded portion of the receipt read correctly (though likely helped by quantity=1, so amount equals unit price — not necessarily proof of fold robustness in general).

**Fixes**

Added five rules to the system instruction addressing the findings above: explicit year-reading care, including occluded line items with illegible fields instead of dropping them, folding discount lines into the discounted item's amount, preferring printed vendor text over logo inference, and a math-based consistency check (prefer whichever subtotal candidate, when added to tax, comes closest to matching total) to resolve DPP-vs-subtotal ambiguity.

Re-tested receipt\_016, receipt\_018, receipt\_019, receipt\_014, and receipt\_025, checked against the physical receipts (not just JSON output):

receipt\_016: year now correctly reads 2026; discount math confirmed correct against the physical receipt.

receipt\_018: the previously-dropped, handwriting-covered item now appears — and better than expected, it's read correctly rather than just marked illegible. Discount consolidation confirmed correct, including the item with two stacked discounts.

receipt\_019: subtotal now correctly resolves to the DPP-derived value rather than the tax-inclusive "subtotal" line, matching what's physically more accurate. The small rounding gap between subtotal+tax and total is real, present on the receipt itself, not a system error.

receipt\_14: vendor name still resolves to the FamilyMart logo rather than the smaller printed label. Checked against the physical receipt — the logo itself is large, legible stylized text positioned more prominently than the plain label below it, so this is judged as acceptable rather than a rule failure: the underlying intent (prefer clearly legible text, don't guess from an ambiguous logo) is still satisfied. receipt\_025 confirms the fallback direction works as intended — an unclear logo there correctly led to reading the printed text instead.

**Step 7 — Build ground truth (This one took a LOT of time 😭)**

Manually labeled all 26 receipts, one JSON file per receipt in data/ground\_truth/ (matching filenames, multi-part receipts like receipt\_026 grouped into a single entry), reading directly from the physical receipts — never from model output, to avoid anchoring bias.

Each field follows the simplified ground truth schema (value, acceptable\_alternatives, status) — no confidence/reason, since ground truth represents verified truth rather than model uncertainty. acceptable\_alternatives was used on a handful of fields where more than one value is legitimately correct (vendor name being the main case — logo brand vs printed label, consistent with the Step 6 finding on receipt\_014). All fields across the 26 receipts were ultimately labeled as either present or not\_present — no field was marked illegible in the final ground truth, even though a few were initially uncertain during labeling.

Also at this point i realized that rotating the picture in widows’s photos also saves it, so some of the photos ended up rotated differently 😭😭

**Step 8 — Wrap extraction as an API service**

Built src/api/main.py using FastAPI, with three endpoints: GET /health (liveness check), POST /extract (single receipt, accepts one or more images for multi-page receipts), and POST /extract/batch (multiple receipts in one request, processed sequentially — not concurrently, given the tight API quota). Both successful extractions and handled ExtractionErrors return HTTP 200, since these are controlled outcomes, not server errors; HTTP 422 is reserved for malformed requests. Cost and latency are logged per request and returned in a response envelope separate from the extraction result itself.

**![][image19]**

Swagger UI file upload issue: the /extract and /extract/batch endpoints showed the files field as a plain text/array input instead of a file picker. Investigated and confirmed this is a known cosmetic bug in the current FastAPI \+ Swagger UI version combination (a schema format change in recent FastAPI that Swagger UI doesn't render correctly) — not a bug in our code.

**![][image20]**

Tested the API instead via a small Python script (requests.post(..., files={"files": f})). First run, using receipt\_001.jpeg (124 KB, 1200x1600): returned HTTP 200 with a correct extraction (matching the earlier direct-script test) — confirmed the API wrapper works end-to-end — but latency\_seconds was 51.57, unexpectedly slow.

Token accounting gap found in that first run: total\_token\_count (4599) didn't match prompt\_token\_count \+ candidates\_token\_count (2516+1542=4058) — a 541 token gap. Investigated and found response.usage\_metadata exposes thoughts\_token\_count, a field our TokenUsage model wasn't capturing. gemini-3.6-flash performs internal reasoning before answering, and those tokens are billed and included in total\_token\_count but excluded from candidates\_token\_count. Fixed TokenUsage to capture this field.

Root cause of the 51.6s latency, found via the uvicorn server log: that request involved 3 consecutive 503 Service Unavailable responses before a 4th successful attempt — the Step 5 retry/backoff logic working as designed, but adding significant time (1s/2s/4s backoff sleep plus each failed attempt's own duration) on top of a normal call.

![][image21]

Re-ran the same script after the TokenUsage fix, this time with no retries needed: latency\_seconds=14.45, and token fields now reconcile correctly — prompt=2516, candidates=1567, thoughts=1040 → total=5123, matching exactly. This confirms both the fix works and gives a clean single-call latency baseline (14.45s) distinct from the earlier retry-inflated outlier.

**![][image22]**

Implication for Step 12: response metadata doesn't currently record retry count, so before/after latency comparisons for the eventual optimization could be unfair if some calls silently absorb retry overhead while others don't. Worth adding a retry count to the metadata before running that comparison. Also identified a candidate optimization: the SDK may expose a thinking\_budget/effort parameter to constrain reasoning token volume, which drove a meaningful share of both latency and cost on these calls — a more promising lever than image compression, since client-side work (file read, request building, parsing) was confirmed to take under 20ms regardless of image size. Deliberately not acted on yet, deferred to Step 12\.

&nbsp;

&nbsp;

Tested /extract/batch with 3 receipts in one request (receipt\_001 single-image, receipt\_026 two-image/multi-page, receipt\_002 single-image), group\_sizes="1,2,1".

Grouping logic confirmed correct — all 3 receipts were split from the flat file list exactly as expected, including the multi-image one. Results returned in submission order with per-receipt latency, consistent with sequential (not concurrent) processing as designed.

![][image23]

Outcome: receipt\_001 and receipt\_026 both failed with 503 UNAVAILABLE ("This model is currently experiencing high demand") after exhausting all retries; receipt\_002 succeeded. This is a genuine Gemini server-side overload, not our API quota (a 429, which this wasn't) — outside our control. More importantly, this is a real-world confirmation of Step 5's resilience design working as intended: the two failures returned clean ExtractionErrors (with image\_paths and a clear message) instead of crashing, and did not block the third receipt in the same batch from being processed and succeeding.

Cost note: API quota is limited, so this kind of retry-heavy failure scenario eats into it faster than a normal successful run — worth staying mindful of remaining quota during further testing, especially if Gemini's server load stays elevated. Decided to skip retrying to test /extract/batch endpoint, will revisit it later.

**Step 9 — Build the eval harness**

Created scripts/run\_eval\_extractions.py: scans data/ground\_truth/ for receipt IDs, maps each to its image path(s) in Raw Data/ (handling multi-image receipts), and calls extract\_receipt\_with\_usage() for any receipt not yet saved under outputs/eval\_runs/\<run\_id\>/extractions/\<receipt\_id\>.json. Checkpointing is file-existence-based — a saved result (success or ExtractionError) counts as done and is skipped on re-run, so an interrupted run (e.g. hitting a rate limit) can resume cleanly with a different API key without redoing completed work or wasting quota.

&nbsp;

Verified the mapping logic (single-image and multi-page grouping) without making real API calls. Missing image files fall through to the existing invalid\_input failure path rather than being special-cased. Each saved result includes an explicit result\_type tag (ReceiptExtraction/ExtractionError) so the downstream scorer doesn't need to infer the type from shape.

Ran scripts/run\_eval\_extractions.py against all 26 receipts. Hit rate limits (429) partway through multiple times 😭😭 — checkpointing worked as designed: switched API keys across a few different Google accounts when a key's quota ran out, re-ran the same run\_id each time, and completed extractions resumed cleanly from wherever they left off without redoing any already-saved receipts.

All 26 receipts now have saved results under outputs/eval\_runs/default/extractions/, each either a successful ReceiptExtraction or a checkpointed ExtractionError.

**Scoring**

Created scripts/score\_eval.py: compares saved extraction results against data/ground\_truth/, field-by-field with tolerance-aware matching (numeric ±1, string exact-after-normalize, line items aligned by description similarity \+ amount before scoring). Outputs a scorecard with per-field precision/recall plus per-document detail.

First run (default) against all 26 receipts: 88.3% overall field accuracy (627/710). Breakdown: 627 correct, 44 wrong\_value (a real value extracted but not matching ground truth), 2 hallucinated (a value extracted where ground truth says the field isn't present), 36 wrongly\_abstained (extraction marked a field not\_present/illegible where ground truth has a real value), 1 missed\_status. Line item alignment matched perfectly across all 26 receipts (0 unmatched in either direction). Hallucination rate is very low (3/710), consistent with the system's core design goal.

receipt\_001 — 6× wrongly\_abstained unit\_price (all line items). Receipt doesn't print per-unit price; GT computed it via math. Covered by the unit\_price fix already applied.

receipt\_002 — hallucinated vendor\_name: GT was illegible, model actually read it correctly ("Cipork Keriyuk") — this was my fault, GT fixed.

wrong\_value receipt\_number: letter-O vs digit-0, in the bent part of the receipt — understandable misread, accepted as known limitation.

![][image24]

receipt\_003 — 3× wrongly\_abstained unit\_price (same as 001). wrong\_value description: GT had the typo ("Cripsy" instead of "Crispy"), not the extraction — GT fixed.

![][image25]

receipt\_004 — wrong\_value unit\_price: GT had a manual typo — GT fixed.

receipt\_005 — vendor name "Bu Kris Tenggilis" vs extracted "Bu Kris Tenggili", missing the final "s" — genuine minor misread, accepted as known limitation. Possibly picked up from the cashier field, which had the same name — worth noting, not actionable.

![][image26]

receipt\_006 — 5× wrongly\_abstained unit\_price (same pattern). 1× missed\_status unit\_price — I missed a line item, GT fixed immediately. Vendor name correctly identified despite an unreadable logo — possibly inferred from the cashier field ("Seniman Mie Kari Rungkut" vs the shorter "Seniman Mie Kari" used) — interesting observation, not an error, worth noting.

receipt\_008 — wrong\_value vendor\_name: extracted the fuller name including the mall location, which is acceptable — added to acceptable\_alternatives. hallucinated receipt\_number: the "141" extracted is actually a queue/order number, not a receipt number — new prompt fix queued to distinguish the two. wrong\_value description: leading symbol, acceptable — added to acceptable\_alternatives.

receipt\_010 — wrong\_value receipt\_number: extracted includes extra context (cashier name, counter code) beyond the clean number. Unsure what the leading "4.0.25" segment is — noted as a pattern to keep in mind, not acted on yet.

receipt\_011 — wrong\_value subtotal: GT was wrong, not the extraction — the model had correctly applied the subtotal-consistency rule (subtotal+tax=total) and I hadn't re-verified GT against that. GT fixed.

Same vendor as receipt\_010, but receipt\_number matched correctly this time ("T1NN-97349") — interesting, worth keeping in mind as a vendor-specific pattern.

New prompt fix queued: flag ambiguity in reason rather than force an implausible attribution.

**After Fixing The Prompt**

Re-ran extraction and scoring with prompt\_v2 (5 prompt fixes applied: unit\_price computation, SKU stripping, queue-number distinction, full-sequence receipt numbers, discount-attribution ambiguity), plus the scorer's symbol-normalization fix.

Result: 94.2% overall field accuracy (669/710), up from 88.3% (627/710) on default. hallucinated dropped from 3 to 0\. missed\_status dropped from 1 to 0\. wrongly\_abstained dropped from 36 to 3\.

New issue found: unit\_price now has 25 wrong\_value mismatches, all on receipts with discounts (receipt\_012, 016, 018, 025, 026 — the same receipts affected by Step 6's discount-consolidation fix). Every mismatch is negative (extracted \< ground truth). Likely cause: the new unit\_price computation rule (amount ÷ quantity) is using amount after the Step 6 discount rule already reduced it to the post-discount total — so the computed unit\_price reflects a discounted per-unit price, while ground truth consistently use the original (pre-discount) unit price.&nbsp;

The intended design: unit\_price should always be the original pre-discount per-unit price; only amount should reflect a discount. The bug is a conflict between two prompt rules applied at different times — the unit\_price computation rule (amount ÷ quantity) was using the already-discounted amount from the Step 6 discount-consolidation rule, producing an incorrectly discounted unit\_price on all 25 mismatched fields (all on receipts with discounts: 012, 016, 018, 025, 026). Fix queued: derive unit\_price from the original pre-discount price, not the discounted amount; abstain if the original price genuinely can't be recovered.

**After Fixing the Prompt (Again) \- Stopped Here Because of Rate Limitation 😭**

Ran extraction for only the 5 receipts affected by the unit\_price/discount bug (012, 016, 018, 025, 026\)

Result: 97.6% overall field accuracy (693/710), up from 94.2% (669/710) on prompt\_v2.

Results specific to the 5 re-run receipts:

receipt\_016, receipt\_018 — fully correct now, no remaining errors. Confirms the unit\_price/discount fix resolved both cleanly.

receipt\_012 — still broadly wrong: 5 fields off simultaneously (receipt\_number, transaction\_date — another year misread, subtotal, tax, line item amount). This goes beyond the discount-attribution issue the fix targeted — likely the receipt itself is simply hard to read (noted earlier as "crumpled, text disappearing"), not explained by any single rule.

receipt\_025 — 1 new wrongly\_abstained: receipt\_number not extracted, ground truth has a value. Likely because the text has started to disappear like 12

receipt\_026 — receipt\_number is now over-long ("498 49881 6926 498030") — the "extract full sequence" fix may have overshot, concatenating multiple candidate number sequences instead of picking the correct one. 1 line item pair (quantity \+ unit\_price) still abstains.

&nbsp;

Refactored run\_eval\_extractions.py to call the API's /extract endpoint via HTTP instead of importing the extraction function directly — required so the eval harness genuinely runs "against the API" per the brief, not just as a local script. Discriminates ReceiptExtraction vs ExtractionError by checking for the failure\_stage key in the response; connection/non-200 failures are saved as a checkpointed api\_failure, consistent with existing resilience design.

**Step 10 — Dockerize**

Created Dockerfile (Python 3.13-slim) and docker-compose.yml with two services: api (serves via uvicorn, healthcheck on /health) and eval (profile-gated so it only runs via docker compose run \--rm eval, waits for api's healthcheck, mounts data/ground\_truth/, Raw Data/, and outputs/ as volumes).

![][image39]

Verified end-to-end without spending API quota, using the already-complete prompt\_v3 checkpoint: docker compose up \-d api \+ docker compose \--profile eval run \--rm \-e RUN\_ID=prompt\_v3 eval reproduced the exact same scorecard (97.6%, 693/710) as the local run, with all 26 receipts correctly read as cached (zero new API calls). Confirms volume mounts, inter-container networking, and the full extraction→scoring pipeline all work correctly inside Docker — not just that the containers start.

![][image40]

&nbsp;

**Step 11 — Full batch run, scorecard, version comparison**

This step's requirements were met incrementally rather than as a separate isolated task:

Full batch runs: all 26 receipts processed end-to-end three times, under distinct run\_ids (default, prompt\_v2, prompt\_v3), using the checkpoint-and-resume extraction runner.

Scorecard: score\_eval.py produces a runnable scorecard (aggregate \+ per-document) for any run\_id, independent of the API layer.

Version comparison: default (88.3%, 627/710) → prompt\_v2 (94.2%, 669/710) → prompt\_v3 (97.6%, 693/710), each transition driven by specific, documented prompt fixes.

Regression caught in practice, not just in theory: the prompt\_v2 run introduced a real regression — the new unit\_price computation rule conflicted with the Step 6 discount-consolidation rule, producing 25 incorrect unit\_price values on discount-affected receipts. This was caught by the scorecard's field-level breakdown before being accepted, and fixed in prompt\_v3.

Run via Docker: reproduced via docker compose run \--rm eval in Step 10, confirming the harness runs against the live API as required, not just as a local script.

**Step 12 — Apply one optimization, measure impact**

Investigated the google-genai SDK's thinking\_config option, found two distinct mechanisms: thinking\_budget (explicit token count, 0 disables) and thinking\_level (coarser enum: MINIMAL/LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, the newer Gemini-3-style interface). Wired both up as an opt-in config in extract.py (default unchanged, thinking\_config=None).

Ran a small comparison (scripts/test\_thinking\_optimization.py) on 2 receipts — receipt\_001 (simple) and receipt\_026 (complex, multi-image, 23 line items) — across 3 configs: baseline, thinking\_budget=0, thinking\_level=LOW. Baseline calls in this run both failed with 503 UNAVAILABLE (Gemini server-side high demand, same issue seen before) — rather than burning more quota to retry, used the already-saved prompt\_v3 checkpoint data for both receipts as the baseline, since that was run under the same unconstrained default.

**Result**

| receipt | config | latency | Total tokens | Line items |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 001 | baseline&nbsp; | 19.86s&nbsp; | 5022&nbsp; | 6 |
| 001 | thinking\_budget=0&nbsp; | 13.7s&nbsp; | 3972&nbsp; | 6 |
| 001 | thinking\_level=LOW&nbsp; | 8.2s&nbsp; | 3977&nbsp; | 6 |
| 026 | baseline&nbsp; | 36.05s&nbsp; | 13088&nbsp; | 23 |
| 026 | thinking\_budget=0&nbsp; | 27.7s&nbsp; | 6888&nbsp; | 23 |
| 026 | thinking\_level=LOW&nbsp; | 21.9s&nbsp; | 6896&nbsp; | 23 |

&nbsp;

thinking\_level=LOW performed best on both metrics: latency down 58% (receipt\_001) and 39% (receipt\_026); tokens down 21% and 47% respectively. Vendor name, total, and line item count were identical to baseline on both receipts — no accuracy loss observed on this small sample. thinking\_budget=0 also improved over baseline but was consistently slower and more token-hungry than thinking\_level=LOW, suggesting fully disabling thinking forces less efficient reasoning-free generation compared to a constrained-but-present thinking budget.

Note: receipt\_026's line item count (23) matched between baseline and both optimized configs — confirms the count reflects earlier prompt fixes, not something affected by this experiment.

Changed THINKING\_CONFIG in extract.py from None to types.ThinkingConfig(thinking\_level=types.ThinkingLevel.LOW) — now the default behavior for every caller (extract\_receipt(), the API, the eval harness), not just an opt-in experiment. Decision based on the 2-receipt comparison above (58%/39% latency reduction, 21%/47% token reduction, no observed accuracy loss) — not validated against the full 26-receipt dataset, a known limitation of this decision given time/quota constraints.

**Step 13 — Build the custom agentic-dev extension**  
Built scripts/diff\_runs.py: compares two eval runs' saved results, detecting field-level regressions (was correct, no longer is) and improvements (wasn't correct, now is), keyed by ground-truth line-item index for stability across runs. This automates a comparison that was previously done by hand multiple times during Step 9\.

Ran against the full project history: python scripts/diff\_runs.py default prompt\_v3 → 88.3% → 97.6% (+9.3%), 7 regressions, 73 improvements, net \+66. Automatically re-confirmed every regression found manually earlier (receipt\_006 vendor truncation, receipt\_012's broad degradation across 3 fields, receipt\_015 description misread, receipt\_025 receipt\_number regression) and one new one not previously isolated (receipt\_004 line item description, a minor new spacing misread).

Important nuance found: at least 8 of the 73 "improvements" show an identical extracted value between default and prompt\_v3 — only the scoring classification changed, because ground truth or the scorer's symbol normalization was corrected in between, not because the extraction prompt improved (e.g. receipt\_011 subtotal, receipt\_013/019/021 descriptions). The remaining \~65 improvements are genuine extraction changes (the unit\_price computation and SKU-stripping fixes). The 9.3% accuracy gain is therefore a mix of real prompt improvements and ground-truth/scorer corrections, not attributable entirely to the prompt — worth being precise about this distinction in the README rather than overstating the model's improvement.
